posts.title: We Don’t All Experience Threats Equally
posts.description: China I’ve finished the last series of blogs, which explored what a threat is, who decides what it looks like, and how looking for threats as part of your job affects the mind. The next series will explore the implications of threats for different parts of society. It feels like a natural progression: moving from experiencing firsthand what it’s like to work in an environment where you look for threats to understanding the privileged position that this work can create, and the sense of protection it may offer others. Technological advances such as AI (sorry!) can drive digital progress, but they can also exclude people from essential services when those services rely on consistent, reliable internet access. One example is the 2022 White Paper protests in China. During lockdowns imposed by the Chinese government, citizens used social media platforms such as Weibo and WeChat to share their discontent and complain about the economic impact. posts.title: Are We Secure, Or Just Afraid?
posts.description: TRIGGER WARNING This blog discusses violence against women and specifically discusses terrorism and murder. I’ve worked in this industry for so long, I’ve realised that security is supposed to make us feel safe, so why does so much of the language used in security make us feel like we’re constantly in danger? FIREWALL DISCRETIONARY ACCESS CONTROL CYBER ATTACK COMPROMISE VULNERABILITY THREAT BREACH INCIDENT ADVERSARY and finally, KUBER-NET-ES , whatever that is. Anyway, you get the point. The careful usage of language in security goes a very long way towards actually making us safe, the problem being that security requires constant attention to dangers. However, we’ve learnt that paying too much attention can change the way you experience the world, a paradox where vigilance meets safety desires. posts.title: What Happens When Looking for Threats Becomes Your Job?
posts.description: So we have spent two posts talking about threats and barely any mention of the folks doing the looking! Now lets begin, the absurdity of life brings opportunities and with those opportunities come threats, now threats have been discussed from a security point of view, now security in its current definition is the authority of being protected from harm, danger, and/or loss along with actions that help keep people, assets and places safe. This short paragraph goes some way towards covering an entire domain of specialism around Security, but i barely touch the surface with it. Police, Intel Analysts, Soldiers, Security Guards, Emergency workers, Abuse investigators, Fraud investigators, Journalists, Parents, Teachers. I could list many, many more but, its boils down to anyone who’s environment teaches them to anticipate and protect from what is considered a dangerous facet of society.
